headline: Instacart launches Clementine AI shopping assistant to help decide meals
summary: The AI chatbot understands natural language to suggest recipes, restock staples, and even turn handwritten lists into carts, but watch your average basket size.
details: Instacart has launched Clementine, its new AI shopping assistant, designed to simplify grocery shopping by helping users decide what to cook and manage their budget. It's now available across North America on the Instacart Marketplace.

Clementine understands natural language prompts, allowing users to request recipes based on dietary needs, protein content, or meal type. It then provides a recipe with an ingredient list that can be added to the cart with a single tap.

The assistant ensures recipe suggestions are based on items currently available at the user's chosen store, preventing the frustration of unavailable ingredients. Users can also remove items they already have from the suggested ingredient list.

Users can customize Clementine's suggestions by setting preferences for nut-free, vegetarian, or gluten-free meals. It can also help restock pantry staples or shop for usual items by referencing past orders.

Clementine can even convert a handwritten grocery list or recipe photo into an item list ready for cart addition. However, Instacart notes that orders placed with Clementine tend to exceed the average basket size of $115.
This launch follows Instacart's previous collaborations with tech companies to integrate grocery shopping with platforms like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Google Search's AI Mode.
